newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: FORECAST-Portugal's yr/yr CPI seen under two pct.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Portugal's yr/yr CPI seen under two pct.

text.p: Portugal's year-on-year inflation rate could hit a new 30-year low below two percent in April, according to a Reuter poll of eight analysts.

The month-on-month rise in the consumer price index (CPI) was forecast at between 0.1 and 0.4 percent giving a year-on-year increase of 1.7-2.0 percent, down from a year-on-year level of 2.5 percent in March.
Five analysts agreed in seeing a month-on-month rise of 0.2 percent and a year-on-year increase of 1.8 percent.
The National Statistics Institute (INE) must issue the April CPI data by April 15.
The principal reason for the sharp slowing was the fact that the jump in meat prices in spring 1996 provoked by the mad cow disease scare had dropped out of the index.
Meat price rises were estimated to have added 0.6 percent to the index in April 1996 when the year-on-year rise was 2.9 percent.

The rolling 12-month average was seen slowing to 3.1 percent in April if the year-on-year rose below two percent. If the rate was two percent, the average would remain unchanged at the 3.2 percent seen in March.
The analysts also forecast a further slowing in price rises of non-tradable goods, mainly wages, to below the 4.5 percent year-on-year rise registered in March.
